name: Attila's Invasion of Gaul and Italy
summary: Attila the Hun's massive invasion of Gaul is halted at the Battle of the Catalaunian Fields (Châlons) by a Roman-Visigoth coalition under Aetius. The following year Attila invades Italy, reaching Milan, but withdraws, possibly due to plague, famine, or Pope Leo I's famous embassy. Attila dies in 453; the Hunnic empire collapses within years.

_quarry.structural_significance: The last major Roman military victory in the west; Aetius's subsequent murder by Valentinian III eliminates the last capable western commander; the Hunnic collapse pushes further Germanic peoples into Roman territory.
